increment_paragraph: **OPENSSL-EX-DATA-REGISTRY (2026-11-19).** User decision 2026-11-19 launches the follow-up OPENSSL-UNSTATED-CALLBACK-SLOTS recorded. CRYPTO_get_ex_new_index (3.5) runs a class's new callbacks when an object of the class is allocated and its free callbacks when one is freed (BIO, DH, DSA, EC_KEY, ENGINE, EVP_PKEY, RSA, SSL, SSL_CTX, SSL_SESSION, UI, UI_METHOD, X509, X509_STORE, X509_STORE_CTX); only eight quirin-provider-openssl declarations named them. The follow-up's second discharge lands: every declaration that allocates, copies or finally frees an object of an ex_data class, directly or as a replaced or temporary object it frees inside, names openssl_ex_data_callbacks (30 declarations, 29 newly: the constructors SSL_CTX_new, SSL_new, X509_new, BIO_new_file, ENGINE_by_id, the PEM readers and d2i_PKCS12_bio; the frees SSL_free, SSL_CTX_free, BIO_free, X509_free, X509_STORE_free, EVP_PKEY_free, ENGINE_free, PKCS12_free, EVP_MD_CTX_free; the handshake and I/O calls, SSL_shutdown, SSL_set_accept_state (RECORD_LAYER_reset creates memory BIOs), the SSL_CTX_use_* loaders, SSL_CTX_load_verify_locations, SSL_CTX_set_default_verify_paths and OPENSSL_init_ssl). The checker's audit table EX_DATA_AUDIT reads each with its classes; a constructor or free left out of the audit, a dropped premise or an unaudited premise refuses (ex_data_audited). C04.18 amended; no gateway rule or route change. Lean: new QCore.OpensslExDataPremise, audited. contracts.lock changes exactly the 29 digests; both load paths unchanged. The predecessor fixture is unchanged (113 bindings, all Pending). Opt-in current over Fluent Bit 046accf6 (base 062974679 vs tip f3db96675): 1098 Safe / 2 Pending / 3699 Unknown / 5 Unsafe in both, no row moved, no row changed content, bindings 113 all Pending, as predicted; the premise is published only in the units' reading-site environment texts. The registry reading itself (a run-wide set per class) needs a literal-keyed registration, an object-less invocation and an invocation beside a reference drop, so it is registered narrower as OPENSSL-EX-DATA-CLASS-REGISTRY. Pinned routes read no user load path: no move predicted, measure --declared deferred to the integrator.

ledger.title: Read the OpenSSL ex_data registry as a run-wide closed set per class
ledger.text: Recorded by OPENSSL-EX-DATA-REGISTRY, which named openssl_ex_data_callbacks on every constructor and free of an ex_data class instead. The premise could be narrowed by reading the registry: a run-wide closed set over CRYPTO_get_ex_new_index's new, dup and free actuals (the SSL_get_ex_new_index family are macros over it in 3.x), keyed by the class_index literal (a non-constant class refuses), invoked at the class's constructors and frees with the data the callback receives. Four things the vocabulary lacks: a registration keyed by a literal integer argument rather than an object's slot (C04.19.3 needs a holder pointer); an invocation with no object parameter (X509_new, SSL_CTX_new's store); an invocation beside a reference drop or release (C04.19 admits none; OPENSSL-FREE-SESSION-REMOVE-INVOCATION changes that rule for the frees); and the free callback's ptr argument, the value an undeclared CRYPTO_set_ex_data / SSL_set_ex_data kept, which only an identity candidate (or a stated retention) could take. The premise P-OPAQUE-SLOT-WRITERS' analogue is that every unit registering an index is in the run. At Fluent Bit 046accf6 the only callers are nghttp2's neverbleed (RSA and EC_KEY free callbacks), outside the production compile database, so the reading would move no measured row. DISCHARGE: the vocabulary and route above with Lean, or keep the premise. Size: large.
